chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ja'far ibn Yahya al-Khuza'i from his father Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār who said:

I entered upon Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) and informed him that a boy had been born to me. He said, 'Did you not name him Muḥammad?' I said, 'I have done so.' He said, 'Then do not strike Muḥammad nor curse him; may God make him a delight of your eyes in your life and a faithful successor after you.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, in which professions should I place him?' He said, 'When you keep him free from five things, place him wherever you wish: Do not make him a money-changer (ṣayrāfī), for the money-changer is not safe from usury (ribā); and do not make him a seller of shrouds, for the seller of shrouds rejoices in the plague when it occurs; and do not make him a seller of food, for he is not safe from hoarding (iḥtikār); and do not make him a butcher, for mercy is stripped from the butcher; and do not make him a slave-dealer (nakhkhās), for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'The worst of people is the one who sells people.'

key_terms.قُرَّةَ عَيْنٍ: Delight of the eyes (source of joy)

ai.seo_question: What are the five professions Imam al-Sadiq advised against for one's children and why?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) provides a nuanced ethical framework for vocational selection, linking specific trades to distinct spiritual vulnerabilities such as usury (*riba*), emotional detachment (*ghilzah*), and exploitation (*ihtikar*). This guidance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and moral character (*akhlaq*) as integral to professional life, ensuring that one’s livelihood does not compromise religious integrity or social justice.
